opening_time.why: Clock spent in the first ten moves is clock missing in the critical middlegame, where the games are decided.
opening_time.action: Drill your repertoire until moves 1–8 are automatic; aim for under 15% of the clock by move 10.

time_trouble.why: Under 10% of the starting time the error rate climbs steeply, whatever the position.
time_trouble.action: Set a checkpoint: at move 30 you must have at least a third of your clock left. If not, play faster, simpler moves until you do.

blunders_low_clock.why: Blunders under a minute are not calculation errors but speed errors: the same player sees the tactic with time.
blunders_low_clock.action: Before every move with under 60 seconds, run the three-second scan: checks, captures, threats, then play.

fast_blunders.why: A move played in under five seconds in a sharp position skips the calculation entirely.
fast_blunders.action: In tense positions, sit on your hands: name the opponent's threat out loud (in your head) before you touch a piece.

long_thinks.why: A very long think that still ends in a mistake means the candidate moves were wrong, not the depth.
long_thinks.action: Cap your thinks: list three candidates first, then calculate; if nothing is clear after a few minutes, play the safest candidate.

tilt.why: After a loss the next game is played with a different goal, revenge, and that goal loses games.
tilt.action: Rule: after two losses in a row, stop playing for the day and review one of the losses instead.

fatigue.why: Attention drops with each game in a session; the later games are played by a weaker version of you.
fatigue.action: Play at most two or three games per session, then do puzzles or a review instead of a fourth game.

conversion.why: A winning position is not a point yet; the drop usually comes from playing for more instead of simplifying.
conversion.action: When ahead, trade pieces, not pawns; ask before every move what the opponent's last swindle could be.

resilience.why: Lost positions are saved by stubborn defence far more often than players expect; resigning early gives away half points.
resilience.action: In a lost position, find the opponent's most unpleasant plan and make it as hard as possible; set one problem per move.

premature_resignation.why: The engine still rated these positions as holdable; the result was decided by the resignation, not the moves.
premature_resignation.action: Never resign on a feeling: resign only when you can name the concrete winning plan for the opponent.
